note: SSOT for the capability-expansion cycles - the P-cycles that grow this factory. A cycle is one round of capability expansion/deepening/update/evolution: it reads the gap surface, ranks candidates, ships slices, and must satisfy the definition-of-done below before it is recorded as done. Every id in a cycle's `added` block is re-checked against the live SSOT by `harness cycle audit`; anything a cycle deliberately did NOT add is a `roadmap` entry with a reason and a revisit trigger, so deferrals cannot be silently forgotten. The cycle ids follow `tasks/PLAN.md` (the single naming authority); PLAN's `P2` sub-slices are folded in here by content, and rounds before P6 are collapsed into `baseline` because they were not recorded while they ran (git history is the record).

definition_of_done.check: every id in a cycle's `added.capabilities` / `added.domains` / `added.references` exists in the live SSOT (`data/*.json`, `review/references.md`), and every `added.clauses` label is anchored in its own module

the trigger is one the engine can actually evaluate (`any` / `min_horizon` / a feature axis / `domain`; an undeclared predicate would silently never fire), and the capability is not a duplicate registration (same `when`, `modules` and title = consolidate, don't add)
the capability's module clauses are real: each claimed `M<k>.<n>` label is anchored in that module's `core/` doc (`M2` -> `core/03`, ...), either as a heading or inside a bold clause title
a stdlib unittest under `tests/` fails if the wiring is removed (the capability or clause is mentioned there)
`sources/source-map.md` maps the clause to a first-party source (arXiv ID / DOI / official repo or doc)
`reference/capability-router.md` routes an intent to the capability, so a reader can find it from a situation
the doc that owns the pattern is listed by `harness skill` (the load index), so one instruction reaches it

roadmap.title_en: Add a redundancy-ratio or module-count metric for this repository
